## Design

### 2026-10-25 – ### What I worked on:

**1.4h**

### What I worked on:
- Brainstormed ideas for Week 3 (Design Your Instrument) and settled on the "Retro Stylophone" – a compact handheld synth using an ESP32.
- Decided against mechanical tactile switches for the keyboard and chose capacitive PCB touch pads instead (using the ESP32 built-in touch peripheral on GPIOs) to save cost and avoid mechanical soldering clutter.
- Set up the GitHub repository `Retro_Stylophone` and organized the initial project structure.
- Calculated the Bill of Materials (BoM) under the Tier 1 grant limit ($30.00). Sourced full multipacks (2x ESP32 boards, 10x 10k potentiometers, 40x slide switches) via Amazon to avoid import duties and split self-funded parts (custom JLCPCB manufacturing and buzzers) transparently.
- Drew the initial concept sketch (top-down view) on paper:
  - Form factor planned at 120 x 70 mm.
  - Layout arranged with the ESP32 on the left, central piezo buzzer, pitch/modulation pot on the right, and a 13-pad keyboard (8 naturals, 5 accidentals) along the bottom edge.
